This FOMC statement signals a pro-growth but risk-aware stance: policy rates remain at the effective lower bound with continued large-scale purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B MBS), while acknowledging improved activity and employment amid vaccinations. Consistent with Taylor-rule style reaction functions and natural-rate-based objectives, slack in the labor market and earlier persistent undershooting of 2% justify holding the nominal policy rate near zero. The shift to average-inflation targeting and the explicit tolerance for inflation “moderately above 2%” align with inflation-forecast targeting insights (Svensson; Woodford) aimed at anchoring expectations at 2% and reducing inflation bias under discretion (Clarida; Orphanides). Describing current inflation as “transitory” reflects the literature’s guidance to accommodate temporary supply shocks rather than over-tighten. Continued asset purchases support accommodative financial conditions and, per the empirical literature, help compress term premia and influence the slope of the yield curve. Overall tone is moderately positive on growth with credible commitment to accommodation, tempered by pandemic-related risks.
